category.name: Cloud identity & SSO
category.description: Identity attacks across Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace, and Duo: token theft, MFA abuse, OAuth consent, federation persistence, and admin takeover.

playbooks.name: Impossible travel sign-in for a single user
playbooks.summary: Use when one user successfully signs in from two distant locations faster than travel allows, in Entra ID, Okta, or Google Workspace logs.

preparation: Ingest Entra sign-in logs, Okta System Log, and Google login audit into the SIEM
Maintain a lookup of corporate VPN egress and SASE IP ranges
Know how to revoke sessions in each IdP for a single user
identification: Compare the two sign-in IPs, ASNs, and user agents against the user's 30-day history
Rule out VPN, SASE, or mobile carrier egress as the cause of the second location
Check whether MFA was satisfied or a token was replayed for the distant sign-in
Contact the user out of band to confirm their actual location
containment: Revoke the user's sessions and refresh tokens in the IdP
Reset the user's password if the distant sign-in is not theirs
Block the suspicious IP in a named location or network zone
eradication: Review mailbox rules, OAuth grants, and MFA methods added from the suspicious session
Remove any devices registered from the suspicious location
Re-register MFA methods with the user present
recovery: Confirm the user can sign in from their real location after reset
Monitor the account for new-country sign-ins for 14 days
Close the alert with the verified cause recorded
lessons: Tune impossible travel rules with known VPN egress to cut false positives
Report the true positive rate of impossible travel alerts
Consider sign-in risk conditional access for unfamiliar locations

splunk.title: Successful sign-ins by country for the user
splunk.spl: index=azure sourcetype="azure:aad:signin" userPrincipalName="<suspect_user>" status.errorCode=0 | iplocation ipAddress | table _time, ipAddress, Country, City, appDisplayName, userAgent | sort _time

splunk.title: Okta sign-ins for the user with geo
splunk.spl: index=okta sourcetype="okta:im2" eventType="user.session.start" actor.alternateId="<suspect_user>" | table _time, client.ipAddress, client.geographicalContext.country, client.userAgent.rawUserAgent, outcome.result

playbooks.name: Stolen session cookie or PRT replayed to bypass MFA
playbooks.summary: Use when a session token, cookie, or Primary Refresh Token is used from a new device or IP without a fresh MFA prompt, often after infostealer malware or AiTM phishing.

preparation: Enable token protection or continuous access evaluation for supported apps
Collect Entra non-interactive sign-in logs, not just interactive
Deploy EDR detections for browser cookie database access by non-browser processes
identification: Find non-interactive sign-ins sharing the user's session ID from a new IP or ASN
Check the user's endpoint for infostealer activity or AiTM phishing clicks
Compare device ID and compliance state between original and replayed sessions
List resources accessed by the replayed session such as mail, files, and admin portals
containment: Revoke all refresh tokens and sessions for the user
Disable the device object if a PRT from that device was stolen
Block the attacker IP in conditional access named locations
eradication: Reimage the endpoint that leaked the token
Reset the user password and any credentials saved in the browser
Remove inbox rules, OAuth consents, or MFA methods created by the attacker
recovery: Re-register the device and require compliant device for the user's sign-ins
Monitor for further session ID reuse from new IPs
Confirm continuous access evaluation is enforced for Exchange and SharePoint
lessons: Add detection for one session ID used from multiple ASNs
Track infostealer infections and their link to token theft
Evaluate phishing-resistant MFA to reduce AiTM token capture

splunk.title: Session ID used from multiple IPs
splunk.spl: index=azure sourcetype="azure:aad:signin" userPrincipalName="<suspect_user>" | stats dc(ipAddress) as ips values(ipAddress) as addrs values(deviceDetail.deviceId) as devices by sessionId | where ips > 1

splunk.title: Browser cookie store access by non-browser processes
splunk.spl: index=sysmon sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode IN (10,11) (TargetFilename="*\\Network\\Cookies" OR TargetFilename="*\\Login Data") NOT Image IN ("*\\chrome.exe","*\\msedge.exe","*\\firefox.exe") | table _time, host, Image, TargetFilename

splunk.title: Okta session reuse from new IPs
splunk.spl: index=okta sourcetype="okta:im2" actor.alternateId="<suspect_user>" | stats dc(client.ipAddress) as ips values(client.ipAddress) as addrs by authenticationContext.externalSessionId | where ips > 1

playbooks.name: New MFA method registered by an attacker
playbooks.summary: Use when a phone number, authenticator app, or FIDO key is added to a user's account from an unfamiliar location or right after a suspicious sign-in.

preparation: Alert on MFA method registration in Entra audit logs and Okta factor enrollment events
Require MFA or a Temporary Access Pass to register new security info
Restrict security info registration to trusted locations or compliant devices
identification: Find the audit event registering the new method and the IP and user agent used
Correlate the registration with the preceding sign-in and its risk level
Ask the user whether they added the method
Check whether the new method was then used to satisfy MFA from a new location
containment: Delete the attacker-registered MFA method
Revoke sessions and reset the user password
Require re-registration of all methods with identity verification
eradication: Check other users for methods registered from the same IP or device
Remove mailbox rules and app consents created during the session
Block the phone number or device used across the tenant if possible
recovery: Confirm the user's remaining methods are all theirs
Monitor for new method registrations on the account for 30 days
Verify conditional access for security info registration is enforced
lessons: Add detection for method registration within an hour of a risky sign-in
Count accounts where attackers registered methods successfully
Review whether registration policy allowed untrusted networks

splunk.title: Entra security info registrations
splunk.spl: index=azure sourcetype="azure:aad:audit" activityDisplayName IN ("User registered security info","User registered all required security info","Admin registered security info") | table _time, targetResources{}.userPrincipalName, initiatedBy.user.ipAddress, additionalDetails{}.value

splunk.title: Okta factor enrollments
splunk.spl: index=okta sourcetype="okta:im2" eventType IN ("user.mfa.factor.activate","system.mfa.factor.activate") | table _time, actor.alternateId, client.ipAddress, target{}.displayName, outcome.result

playbooks.name: MFA push fatigue ends in an approved attacker sign-in
playbooks.summary: Use when a user receives a burst of push MFA prompts and eventually approves one, granting an attacker who holds the password access to the account.

preparation: Enable number matching and location context for push MFA in Entra, Okta, and Duo
Give users a one-click way to report unexpected MFA prompts
Alert on more than five denied or timed-out pushes for a user in an hour
identification: Count denied, timed-out, and approved push events for the user in the window
Identify the source IP of the sign-in that triggered the approved push
Interview the user about the approval and any phone calls received
Review what the attacker session accessed after approval
containment: Revoke the user's sessions and reset the password the attacker held
Temporarily disable push and require a phishing-resistant method for the user
Block the source IP across the IdP
eradication: Remove MFA methods, app passwords, or devices added after the approval
Check how the password was obtained such as reuse, phishing, or infostealer
Search for the same source IP pushing other users
recovery: Re-enable MFA with number matching for the user
Monitor the account for unusual push volume for 14 days
Brief the user on reporting unexpected prompts
lessons: Track the rate of approved pushes after repeated denials
Move high-risk groups to FIDO2 or passkeys
Add MFA fatigue examples to security awareness training

splunk.title: Duo push burst for one user
splunk.spl: index=duo sourcetype="cisco:duo:authentication" factor=duo_push user.name="<suspect_user>" | bin _time span=1h | stats count(eval(result="denied")) as denied count(eval(result="success")) as approved values(access_device.ip) as ips by _time

splunk.title: Okta Verify push denials then success
splunk.spl: index=okta sourcetype="okta:im2" eventType="system.push.send_factor_verify_push" OR eventType="user.authentication.auth_via_mfa" actor.alternateId="<suspect_user>" | stats count by eventType, outcome.result, client.ipAddress

splunk.title: Entra MFA denials by user
splunk.spl: index=azure sourcetype="azure:aad:signin" status.errorCode IN (500121,50074) | bin _time span=1h | stats count by _time, userPrincipalName | where count > 5

playbooks.name: Illicit OAuth app consent grants mailbox or file access
playbooks.summary: Use when a user or admin consents to an unfamiliar multi-tenant app requesting scopes like Mail.Read, Files.ReadWrite.All, or offline_access.

preparation: Restrict user consent to verified publishers and low-risk permissions
Enable the admin consent workflow for everything else
Ingest Entra audit logs for Consent to application events
identification: Find Consent to application events and list app ID, publisher, and scopes granted
Identify all users who consented to the same app
Review the app's sign-in activity and Graph API calls in service principal sign-in logs
Check the reply URL domain and app creation date for signs of a malicious app
containment: Disable the service principal for the app in the tenant
Revoke OAuth2 permission grants for all consenting users
Revoke refresh tokens of the consenting users
eradication: Delete the service principal after evidence capture
Review mailbox and OneDrive access by the app for data exposure
Report the malicious app to Microsoft
recovery: Confirm no remaining grants exist for the app ID
Notify affected users and data owners of exposure
Monitor for new consents to apps from the same publisher
lessons: Add detection for consent to apps with high-privilege scopes
Review consent settings that allowed the grant
Track number of user-consented apps in the tenant

splunk.title: Consent to application events
splunk.spl: index=azure sourcetype="azure:aad:audit" activityDisplayName="Consent to application" | spath path=targetResources{}.modifiedProperties{}.newValue output=scopes | table _time, initiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName, targetResources{}.displayName, scopes

splunk.title: O365 activity by the app
splunk.spl: index=o365 sourcetype="o365:management:activity" AppId="<app_id>" | stats count by Operation, UserId, ClientIP

playbooks.name: Secret or certificate added to a service principal
playbooks.summary: Use when a new client secret or certificate is added to an app registration or service principal, giving the attacker non-interactive, MFA-free access to its permissions.

preparation: Alert on Add service principal credentials and certificate events in Entra audit logs
Inventory high-privilege app registrations and their owners
Limit who can manage application credentials
identification: Find the audit event adding the credential and the actor and IP
List the app roles and Graph permissions the service principal holds
Review service principal sign-in logs for use of the new credential
Confirm with the app owner whether the credential is expected
containment: Remove the attacker-added secret or certificate
Disable the service principal if actively abused
Revoke tokens issued to the service principal
eradication: Audit all credentials on the app and remove any others that are unexplained
Review resources the service principal accessed for data exposure
Reset credentials of the actor account that added the secret
recovery: Confirm the app still functions with only legitimate credentials
Monitor service principal sign-ins for unexpected IPs
Verify credential management is limited to owners
lessons: Detect credential additions to privileged service principals
Report app registrations with secrets expiring beyond policy
Review whether managed identities could replace static secrets

splunk.title: Service principal credential additions
splunk.spl: index=azure sourcetype="azure:aad:audit" activityDisplayName IN ("Add service principal credentials","Update application - Certificates and secrets management") | table _time, initiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName, initiatedBy.user.ipAddress, targetResources{}.displayName

splunk.title: Non-interactive sign-ins by the service principal
splunk.spl: index=azure sourcetype="azure:aad:signin" servicePrincipalName="<app_name>" | stats count by ipAddress, resourceDisplayName, status.errorCode

playbooks.name: Global Administrator or privileged role newly assigned
playbooks.summary: Use when a user is granted Global Admin, Privileged Role Admin, or another high-tier Entra role without a change request, indicating privilege escalation.

preparation: Alert on Add member to role events for privileged directory roles
Manage privileged roles through PIM with approval and time limits
Keep a baseline of standing Global Admin assignments
identification: Identify who assigned the role, to whom, and whether via PIM activation or direct add
Confirm a change ticket exists for the assignment
Review what the newly privileged user did after assignment
Check whether the assigning account was itself recently compromised
containment: Remove the unauthorized role assignment
Revoke sessions for both the assignee and the assigner
Reset passwords and re-verify MFA for both accounts
eradication: Review all tenant changes the assignee made with the role
Remove persistence such as new apps, secrets, or federation changes
Audit other recent privileged role changes for the same pattern
recovery: Reconcile current role holders against the approved baseline
Re-enable legitimate accounts after review
Monitor privileged role assignment events at high sensitivity
lessons: Enforce PIM with approval for all Global Admin activations
Measure count of standing versus eligible privileged assignments
Review how the assigner obtained the rights to grant the role

splunk.title: Privileged role assignments
splunk.spl: index=azure sourcetype="azure:aad:audit" activityDisplayName="Add member to role" | spath path=targetResources{}.modifiedProperties{} | search "Global Administrator" OR "Privileged Role Administrator" | table _time, initiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName, targetResources{}.userPrincipalName

splunk.title: Actions by the new admin
splunk.spl: index=azure sourcetype="azure:aad:audit" initiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName="<suspect_user>" | stats count by activityDisplayName, result | sort - count

playbooks.name: Conditional access policy disabled or weakened
playbooks.summary: Use when a conditional access policy enforcing MFA or device compliance is disabled, scoped out, or set to report-only, removing a control attackers want gone.

preparation: Alert on Update and Delete conditional access policy events
Export and version all conditional access policies nightly
Restrict policy editing to a small, monitored admin group
identification: Find the policy change event, the actor, and the before and after state
Determine which control was removed such as MFA or compliant device
Identify sign-ins that benefited from the gap during the change window
Confirm whether a change ticket covers the modification
containment: Re-enable or restore the policy from the saved baseline
Revoke sessions for the actor who made the change
Reset the actor password if the change is unauthorized
eradication: Review all policy changes by the actor for other weakenings
Investigate sign-ins that bypassed MFA during the gap
Remove any accounts or apps excluded from policies without justification
recovery: Confirm policies match the approved baseline and are enforcing
Monitor conditional access change events closely for 30 days
Validate MFA enforcement with a test sign-in
lessons: Add detection for CA policies set to disabled or report-only
Require change tickets and dual approval for CA edits
Track the number of accounts excluded from MFA policies

splunk.title: Conditional access policy changes
splunk.spl: index=azure sourcetype="azure:aad:audit" activityDisplayName IN ("Update conditional access policy","Delete conditional access policy","Disable Strong Authentication") | table _time, initiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName, initiatedBy.user.ipAddress, targetResources{}.displayName

splunk.title: Sign-ins without MFA during the change window
splunk.spl: index=azure sourcetype="azure:aad:signin" earliest=<change_start> latest=<change_end> authenticationRequirement=singleFactorAuthentication status.errorCode=0 | stats count by userPrincipalName, appDisplayName, ipAddress

playbooks.name: Federation trust or domain added for Golden SAML persistence
playbooks.summary: Use when a new federated domain or trust is added in Entra ID, letting an attacker with the token-signing key forge SAML assertions for any user.

preparation: Alert on Set domain authentication and Add partner to federation events
Baseline all federated domains and their legitimate IdP endpoints
Protect AD FS token-signing certificates and monitor their export
identification: Find the domain federation change event, actor, and the new issuer URI
Verify whether the federated domain and issuer are legitimate
Look for sign-ins asserting the new or modified federated domain
Check AD FS servers for token-signing key export if federation is on-prem
containment: Remove the rogue federated domain or revert it to managed authentication
Revoke sessions tenant-wide for likely impersonated accounts
Rotate the AD FS token-signing certificate if it may be compromised
eradication: Reset the actor account and review other federation and domain changes
Audit sign-ins that used forged assertions for data access
Rebuild AD FS and rotate all signing material if key theft is confirmed
recovery: Confirm only legitimate federated domains remain configured
Monitor federation configuration events for 30 days
Validate real federation still authenticates users
lessons: Detect any domain authentication type change in Entra
Move eligible domains to cloud-managed authentication
Track token-signing certificate rotation cadence

splunk.title: Domain federation changes
splunk.spl: index=azure sourcetype="azure:aad:audit" activityDisplayName IN ("Set domain authentication","Add unverified domain","Set federation settings on domain") | table _time, initiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName, targetResources{}.displayName, modifiedProperties{}.newValue

splunk.title: Sign-ins using the federated domain
splunk.spl: index=azure sourcetype="azure:aad:signin" | spath path=authenticationDetails{}.authenticationMethod output=method | search userPrincipalName="*@<federated_domain>" | stats count by userPrincipalName, ipAddress, method

playbooks.name: Okta admin console access by an unauthorized account
playbooks.summary: Use when an Okta super admin or org admin performs sensitive changes from an unfamiliar IP or device, or a new admin is granted rights without approval.

preparation: Stream the Okta System Log to the SIEM with admin role grant events
Restrict admin console access by network zone and require phishing-resistant MFA
Keep a baseline of super admin and org admin assignments
identification: Review user.account.privilege.grant events and who granted admin rights
Check admin actions from IPs or devices outside the admin network zone
List policy, app, and user changes made in the suspicious admin session
Confirm the admin assignment against change records
containment: Revoke the unauthorized admin role and clear the account's sessions
Reset the account password and reset its MFA factors
Restrict admin console access to a trusted network zone
eradication: Revert configuration changes made in the session such as IdP, policy, or app edits
Review all admin grants for other unauthorized assignments
Reset credentials of the account that performed the grant
recovery: Reconcile admin role holders against the baseline
Monitor admin actions from new IPs for 30 days
Confirm network zone and MFA controls are enforced on the console
lessons: Alert on admin role grants and admin actions from untrusted networks
Reduce standing super admins and add approval for grants
Review how the attacker reached an admin-capable account

splunk.title: Okta admin privilege grants
splunk.spl: index=okta sourcetype="okta:im2" eventType="user.account.privilege.grant" | table _time, actor.alternateId, client.ipAddress, target{}.alternateId, debugContext.debugData.privilegeGranted

splunk.title: Admin console actions from new IPs
splunk.spl: index=okta sourcetype="okta:im2" eventType IN ("policy.lifecycle.update","application.lifecycle.update","system.idp.lifecycle.create") | stats count values(eventType) as actions by actor.alternateId, client.ipAddress

playbooks.name: Okta support HAR file session token abuse
playbooks.summary: Use when session tokens from an uploaded HAR file or support case are replayed against the Okta tenant, letting an attacker impersonate users or admins.

preparation: Teach admins to sanitize HAR files before sharing with any vendor
Bind Okta admin sessions to network and enable session token limits
Stream impersonation and session events to the SIEM
identification: Identify sessions replayed from IPs that differ from where the token was issued
Correlate recent support cases and HAR uploads with the session IDs seen
List admin actions taken by the hijacked sessions
Check which users or admins the tokens belonged to
containment: Revoke all active sessions for affected admins and clear their tokens
Reset passwords and MFA factors for the affected admins
Restrict admin sessions to trusted network zones immediately
eradication: Revert any configuration changes made with the hijacked sessions
Rotate API tokens that may have been exposed in the same cases
Confirm no new IdPs, policies, or admin grants were added
recovery: Shorten admin session lifetimes and require reauthentication
Monitor for replayed session IDs for 30 days
Validate that only sanitized diagnostics are shared going forward
lessons: Add detection for one session token used from multiple IPs
Create a policy for sanitizing diagnostics shared with vendors
Track vendor support interactions as a supply-chain risk

splunk.title: Session token reuse across IPs
splunk.spl: index=okta sourcetype="okta:im2" | stats dc(client.ipAddress) as ips values(client.ipAddress) as addrs values(eventType) as events by authenticationContext.externalSessionId | where ips > 1 AND events="user.session.start"

splunk.title: Admin actions by hijacked sessions
splunk.spl: index=okta sourcetype="okta:im2" authenticationContext.externalSessionId IN (<suspect_sessions>) | table _time, eventType, actor.alternateId, target{}.displayName, client.ipAddress

playbooks.name: Rogue identity provider added in Okta for inbound federation
playbooks.summary: Use when a new external IdP or routing rule is created in Okta so an attacker-controlled IdP can authenticate as existing users via account linking.

preparation: Alert on system.idp.lifecycle.create and routing rule changes in the System Log
Baseline legitimate IdPs and their metadata endpoints
Restrict IdP and routing rule management to a monitored admin group
identification: Review the IdP creation event, actor, and the external IdP issuer and endpoints
Check whether account linking maps external identities to existing Okta users
Find sign-ins that authenticated through the new IdP
Confirm the IdP is not a legitimate new integration
containment: Deactivate and delete the rogue IdP and any routing rule steering to it
Revoke sessions for users who authenticated through it
Reset the actor account that created the IdP
eradication: Review account linking settings abused by the IdP
Audit other IdP and routing rule changes by the actor
Reset passwords for users whose accounts were linked
recovery: Confirm only legitimate IdPs and routing rules remain
Monitor IdP lifecycle events for 30 days
Verify real federated logins still work
lessons: Detect IdP creation and routing rule changes immediately
Review who can manage inbound federation
Track the count of configured IdPs and their owners

splunk.title: Okta IdP lifecycle events
splunk.spl: index=okta sourcetype="okta:im2" eventType IN ("system.idp.lifecycle.create","system.idp.lifecycle.activate","policy.rule.add") | table _time, actor.alternateId, client.ipAddress, target{}.displayName, outcome.result

splunk.title: Sign-ins via the new IdP
splunk.spl: index=okta sourcetype="okta:im2" eventType="user.authentication.auth_via_IDP" | search target{}.displayName="<idp_name>" | stats count by actor.alternateId, client.ipAddress

playbooks.name: Google Workspace super admin account compromised
playbooks.summary: Use when a Google Workspace super admin shows logins from unfamiliar locations or makes sensitive admin console changes without authorization.

preparation: Stream Admin audit and login audit logs to the SIEM
Enforce 2-Step Verification with security keys for all super admins
Keep a baseline of super admin role holders and a break-glass account
identification: Review login audit for the admin's IPs and challenge results
List ADMIN_SETTINGS changes such as added admins, disabled 2SV, or new app passwords
Check for OAuth tokens or app passwords created by the account
Confirm the admin activity against change records
containment: Suspend or reset the compromised super admin and sign out all its sessions
Revoke app passwords and OAuth tokens for the account
Temporarily remove super admin role if a lower role suffices for recovery
eradication: Revert admin console changes made by the account
Remove any new admins or roles the account created
Review Gmail delegation and forwarding added by the account
recovery: Re-enroll the admin with a security key and restore least privilege
Monitor super admin logins and admin changes for 30 days
Verify break-glass account is intact and untouched
lessons: Alert on 2SV disablement and new super admin creation
Reduce the number of standing super admins
Review how the account was phished or credential-stuffed

splunk.title: Super admin logins with geo
splunk.spl: index=gws sourcetype="gws:reports:login" | search "<suspect_user>" | iplocation ipAddress | table _time, email, ipAddress, Country, login_challenge_method, event.name

splunk.title: Admin console changes
splunk.spl: index=gws sourcetype="gws:reports:admin" | search actor.email="<suspect_user>" | table _time, actor.email, event.name, parameters.USER_EMAIL, parameters.ROLE_NAME

playbooks.name: Google domain-wide delegation abused by a service account
playbooks.summary: Use when a service account with domain-wide delegation impersonates many users to read Gmail or Drive, or when new delegation scopes are added in the admin console.

preparation: Inventory service accounts with domain-wide delegation and their scopes
Alert on changes to API client access authorizations in the admin console
Restrict who can manage service accounts in the linked Google Cloud project
identification: Review admin audit for added OAuth client scopes granting delegation
Find Gmail and Drive access events performed by the delegated service account
Count distinct users the service account impersonated
Check the Google Cloud project for a newly added service account key
containment: Remove the domain-wide delegation authorization for the client ID
Disable or delete the service account key used
Revoke tokens issued to the service account
eradication: Rotate remaining keys and remove unneeded delegation scopes
Review which mailboxes and files the service account read
Lock down the Google Cloud project IAM that allowed key creation
recovery: Confirm only approved delegation authorizations remain
Monitor the service account for impersonation activity
Notify data owners of any confirmed access
lessons: Detect new delegation scope authorizations immediately
Report service accounts with broad Gmail or Drive scopes
Review whether delegation is needed or can be scoped per user

splunk.title: Delegation scope authorization changes
splunk.spl: index=gws sourcetype="gws:reports:admin" event.name="AUTHORIZE_API_CLIENT_ACCESS" OR event.name="CHANGE_API_CLIENT_ACCESS" | table _time, actor.email, parameters.API_CLIENT_NAME, parameters.API_SCOPES

splunk.title: Drive access by the service account
splunk.spl: index=gws sourcetype="gws:reports:drive" actor.email="<service_account>" | stats dc(parameters.owner) as users count by event.name | sort - count

playbooks.name: Password spray over legacy authentication protocols
playbooks.summary: Use when attackers spray credentials via legacy protocols like IMAP, POP, SMTP AUTH, or basic auth that bypass modern MFA and conditional access.

preparation: Block legacy authentication with conditional access where possible
Report which users and mailboxes still allow basic auth protocols
Ingest Entra sign-in logs with clientAppUsed detail
identification: Find sign-ins where clientAppUsed is a legacy protocol and group by source IP
Count distinct users targeted by each source over legacy auth
Identify successful legacy sign-ins that bypassed MFA
Map the mailboxes accessed after successful legacy sign-ins
containment: Block the spraying IPs in named locations
Reset passwords for accounts with successful legacy sign-ins
Disable legacy auth protocols for the targeted mailboxes
eradication: Remove mailbox forwarding or rules added via legacy access
Migrate remaining legacy-auth apps to modern authentication
Confirm no app passwords remain for the affected accounts
recovery: Confirm legacy auth is blocked tenant-wide or per mailbox
Monitor for legacy auth sign-in attempts for 30 days
Verify legitimate mail clients use modern auth
lessons: Alert on any successful legacy auth sign-in
Track the count of mailboxes still permitting basic auth
Plan full legacy authentication retirement

splunk.title: Legacy auth spray by source
splunk.spl: index=azure sourcetype="azure:aad:signin" clientAppUsed IN ("IMAP4","POP3","SMTP","Other clients","Authenticated SMTP") | stats dc(userPrincipalName) as users count by ipAddress, clientAppUsed | where users > 10

splunk.title: Successful legacy sign-ins
splunk.spl: index=azure sourcetype="azure:aad:signin" clientAppUsed IN ("IMAP4","POP3","Authenticated SMTP") status.errorCode=0 | table _time, userPrincipalName, ipAddress, clientAppUsed

playbooks.name: Guest or B2B account abused for internal access
playbooks.summary: Use when an external guest account is used to access resources beyond its intended scope, or a flood of guest invitations is sent to establish footholds.

preparation: Restrict who can invite guests and require sponsors for B2B accounts
Alert on bulk guest invitations and guest access to sensitive apps
Run periodic access reviews of guest accounts
identification: List resources the guest accessed and compare against its intended scope
Review who invited the guest and whether a sponsor is recorded
Check for a spike in invitations from one inviter or source IP
Determine whether the guest's home tenant is trusted
containment: Block or delete the abusive guest account
Revoke the guest's sessions and app access
Restrict external collaboration settings to allowlisted domains
eradication: Remove the guest from groups and apps it should not have had
Review other guests invited by the same inviter
Reset the inviter account if the invitations were unauthorized
recovery: Run an access review to confirm remaining guests are justified
Monitor guest sign-ins and resource access for 30 days
Confirm external collaboration settings are tightened
lessons: Alert on guest access to Tier 0 or sensitive applications
Enforce sponsors and expiration on all guest accounts
Track the count of stale guest accounts

splunk.title: Guest invitation spikes
splunk.spl: index=azure sourcetype="azure:aad:audit" activityDisplayName="Invite external user" | bin _time span=1h | stats count by _time, initiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName | where count > 20

splunk.title: Guest sign-ins to sensitive apps
splunk.spl: index=azure sourcetype="azure:aad:signin" userType=Guest appDisplayName IN (<sensitive_apps>) status.errorCode=0 | stats count by userPrincipalName, appDisplayName, ipAddress

playbooks.name: Device code phishing grants attacker a token
playbooks.summary: Use when a user is tricked into entering a device code on a legitimate login page, issuing the attacker a token for the user's account without a password.

preparation: Block device code flow with conditional access except where required
Ingest sign-in logs capturing authenticationProtocol deviceCode
Teach users that legitimate services rarely ask them to enter a device code
identification: Find sign-ins using the device code protocol and the resulting IP and client
Correlate with phishing emails or messages containing a device code prompt
Identify the resources the issued token accessed
